findings.title: Project attribution profile changed without sign-off
findings.problem: activeProfile, the profile name and codeMieProject were rewritten from epm-cdme to epm-cdme-cp (lines 3, 13, 57). codeMieProject feeds X-CodeMie-Project attribution, which security-practices.md and git-workflow.md treat as a change needing recorded security-review sign-off. The edit is unrelated to the EPMCDME-16939 Agent fork_agent_id change.
findings.impact: A silent project-value change can misattribute analytics and usage across projects and breaks the one-logical-change rule. Whether the file is tracked was not confirmed: .codemie is listed in .gitignore, so the edit may be local-only.
findings.recommendation: Revert .codemie/codemie-cli.config.json to its base content if the edit is an accidental local-profile change. If intended, split it into its own change and record the security-review sign-off.

findings.title: Agent background launch result is stamped
findings.problem: resolveForkAgentFields stamps fork_agent_id whenever an Agent result has a string agentId. A background call (run_in_background: true) returns an immediate launch result that already carries agentId, and an error result could echo one. Tests, title and comments say foreground, and no test shows whether such results are intended or excluded.
findings.impact: The launch-time agent.tool.end may be paired with the whole background run or mispaired by the backend. Backend pairing behaviour and the real launch result shape were not confirmed, so reachability and consequence are unverified.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether an Agent result that is a launch acknowledgement or has a status other than completed should carry fork_agent_id. If not, gate the Agent branch on the completed status; if so, pin it with a test and state it in docs/ARCHITECTURE-OTLP-PLUGIN.md.

findings.title: Agent JSON-text result is not read
findings.problem: For Agent, agentId is read only from an object tool_response, while Skill accepts JSON text via parseJsonObject. The spec Approach and Decisions still state a JSON-text tolerance; the plan notes allow dropping it. A test pins that JSON text yields nothing. The only evidence for the object shape is one captured run.
findings.impact: If a Claude Code version or transport delivers the Agent result serialized or wrapped, fork_agent_id is dropped with no log and rows fall back to the parent-window estimate. Whether such a delivery exists was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether an Agent tool_response delivered as JSON text should be read. Either parse it with parseJsonObject as the spec Approach states, or update the spec Approach/Decisions and the architecture doc to say objects only, and keep the pinned test.
